cases.title: A missing or empty required part gives one JSON error and exit 2
cases.given: A scratch git repo with no config, and a repo with branchFormat team/{name:lower}-x.
cases.when: Run name for e2e-area with no --area, with --area '', with no --id, with --id ''; and for slice with no --id and with --id ''.
cases.then: Each run exits 2 and prints one JSON object with ok false and an error that names the missing part.
cases.expected: Exit 2, one JSON object, ok false, the error names area or id, empty stderr, no tree or ref change.
cases.actual: 8 of 8 runs: exit 2, for example {"ok": false, "error": "a e2e-area branch name needs a non-empty area"}; stderr empty; every tree unchanged.
cases.specSource: R-099 acceptance; R-018 quote 'A missing part is a Fail'

cases.title: Hostile --id and --area values are literal text and cause no side effect
cases.given: A repo with the default format and a repo with team/{name:lower}-x.
cases.when: Feed every argv-safe entry of control-chars, traversal, unicode-whitespace, unicode-confusables, format-strings, injection and oversized as --id (slice) and as --id and --area (e2e-area).
cases.then: Each run exits 0 or 2 with one JSON object, no traceback, and no tree or ref change. On success the branch is the literal part in the format.
cases.expected: Every run exits 0 or 2 with one JSON object. Success branches equal 'sdlc/'+value and 'sdlc/'+value+'-e2e-'+value byte for byte.
cases.actual: About 290 runs: all exit 0 with one JSON object; for example --id 'x; touch pwned' gives branch 'sdlc/x; touch pwned' and no file pwned appears; 200k-char values return in one line; every tree unchanged.
cases.specSource: Spec: every command prints one JSON object and exits 0 or 2; R-099 acceptance (no traceback)

seeds.title: name gives git-invalid branch names for hostile parts
seeds.detail: name does not run git check-ref-format on the full name. --id '../..', 'a b', 'HEAD@{1}', '*' and a tab give exit 0 with branches such as 'sdlc/../..', which git check-ref-format --branch refuses. The spec validates only the format. A later slice that creates branches must check the full name.

seeds.title: integer flags accept unicode digits, padding and underscores
seeds.detail: argparse type=int uses Python int(), so --n '٣', '１２', ' 3 ', '\u00a03' and '1_000' are accepted as 3, 12, 3, 3 and 1000. The spec does not say which integer forms are valid. When n, round or part reach a branch name (S-004 to S-006), the name can differ from the operator's text.

seeds.title: invalid UTF-8 in a part gives lone surrogate escapes in the JSON output
seeds.detail: Raw bytes \xff\xfe in --id give branch 'sdlc/\udcff\udcfe' with exit 0. Strict JSON readers can refuse or replace lone surrogates, so a consumer of the branch field can see a different name.

seeds.title: argparse error echoes an oversized value in full
seeds.detail: --round with 100000 digits gives one JSON error that holds all the digits. The spec states no limit, so this goes to verify-limits.

seeds.title: testkit: cli-runner cannot pass raw bytes in argv
seeds.detail: Node spawn takes strings only, so invalid UTF-8 argv needs a Python relay inside the test. A run option for byte arguments would remove that helper.
